title: China is investigating DeepSeek and Moonshot, The Information reports
content:
While the CAC summoned all 7 companies namechecked by Anthropic’s report, the probe quickly zeroed in on DeepSeek and Moonshot due to the examples the report detailed.
Jing Yang wrote that on Tuesday, about her own story. She and Qianer Liu reported for The Information that the Cyberspace Administration of China is investigating both companies over user data that may have reached Anthropic.
Regulators have questioned staff at both. The probe is open and no penalty has been decided. Neither company has commented publicly, and TNW has not independently verified the report.
The Cyberspace Administration is China’s internet regulator. It licenses AI services for the domestic market, polices what leaves the country in the way of data, and can order products withdrawn. A summons from it is not a court proceeding, and it does not need one to act.
What set it off
The trigger was an American company’s document. TNW covered Anthropic’s threat intelligence report on 10 September.
In it, Anthropic said seven China-based labs had been relaying customer requests through Claude to harvest its output. It calls the practice illicit distillation. The seven are Alibaba, Moonshot AI, DeepSeek, Zhipu, MiniMax, Xiaomi and SenseTime.
The report covers misuse Anthropic says it found between December 2025 and August 2026. It logs each campaign under its own case code and describes how the traffic was detected, including the use of fraudulent accounts to spread requests across many identities.
The volumes in the published report come to roughly 190 million exchanges. They are not evenly spread.
Alibaba accounts for more than 151 million, logged between May and July. Moonshot is next at about 23 million across the same months. DeepSeek’s campaign is smaller in total but far denser: more than 12.1 million exchanges inside 14 days in July. Zhipu runs to 3.4 million, and Xiaomi to just over 400,000.
The Moonshot campaign gives a sense of the method. Anthropic counted almost 300,000 requests in a single ten-day window, spread across 5,380 fraudulent accounts. It said Moonshot forwarded the requests silently and showed users the answers as though its own Kimi model had written them.
All seven were summoned. The investigation has settled on the second and third largest.
For Alibaba this is the second accusation in three months. In June, Anthropic accused Alibaba of distilling Claude into its Qwen models, and TNW reported it at the time. Three weeks after that, Alibaba moved to ban Claude Code internally over what it called a backdoor risk to Chinese users.
Why those two
Jing Yang says the probe narrowed because of the examples Anthropic detailed, rather than the totals.
One of those examples, according to The Information, involved a user Anthropic assessed as likely affiliated with the People’s Liberation Army. That user asked Moonshot’s Kimi to analyse surveillance footage following a person across hundreds of police cameras in Chengdu, including cameras outside PLA facilities and defence-linked institutes. Moonshot allegedly passed the request and the footage to Claude without telling the user.
Police camera footage and material tied to defence institutes sit in the categories China’s own cross-border data rules treat most carefully. A lab accused of moving that abroad has a domestic problem before it has an international one.
Our September coverage recorded a related detail from the same report. One relayed query exposed live credentials tied to a Russian defence agency.
Zhipu, a third name on Anthropic’s list, spent last week on an unrelated data problem of its own. It apologised on Monday after a developer found its ZCode tool uploading encrypted snapshots of local code repositories without consent.
Xiaomi, a fourth, released the highest-scoring open-weight model yet published on Tuesday. It has not responded to the Anthropic allegation either.
The complaint has flipped direction
Anthropic’s grievance was about what left Claude. Chinese labs, it said, were taking its model’s output and passing it off as their own.
Beijing’s grievance is the opposite. The regulator’s concern is what went the other way: Chinese users’ data landing on an American company’s servers without those users knowing.
Same alleged conduct, read from the other end. China is not endorsing Anthropic’s complaint. It has found its own inside the same evidence.
Twelve days ago, Beijing called this unfounded
On 10 September, the day Anthropic published, China rejected a US intelligence advisory on Chinese AI distillation as unfounded. The foreign ministry dismissed the accusations in public.
Twelve days later its internet regulator had summoned every company Anthropic named.
Those are two separate documents. The US advisory, published on 9 September by the NSA, FBI and CISA, named six Chinese AI firms. Anthropic’s report, out the following day, described seven. Beijing’s public position addressed the first.
Bad timing for both
DeepSeek is due to brief the Security Council this week on the risks AI poses to international security. TNW reported that on Tuesday. The briefing falls during the UN General Assembly, and Moonshot is among the other companies appearing.
Moonshot has a different problem. It is working towards a Hong Kong listing, and an open regulatory investigation is the kind of thing that has to appear in a prospectus.
Neither company has said anything about the probe. Anthropic has not commented on the fact that its report has prompted a foreign regulator to summon seven companies.
Chinese regulators have not set a timetable and have not said whether they will penalise either company. The largest campaign in Anthropic’s report belongs to a company that is not, for now, the subject of the inquiry.

report.summary: 网信办调查DeepSeek与月之暗面用户数据外流问题
report.background: 事件源于Anthropic于9月10日发布的威胁情报报告，指控阿里、月之暗面、DeepSeek、智谱、MiniMax、小米、商汤七家中国实验室用虚假账号把用户请求转发给Claude、窃取其输出，即所谓的“非法蒸馏”，报告记录约1.9亿次交互。中国网信办随即召见全部七家，随后调查聚焦DeepSeek和月之暗面。耐人寻味的是，Anthropic在意的是模型输出外流，北京在意的是中国用户数据未经知情流向美国服务器——同一批证据，两个方向。而就在报告发布前一天，美国NSA、FBI与CISA刚发布公告点名六家中国AI公司，中国外交部称之为毫无根据。
key_points: 触发点是Anthropic的报告：七家中国实验室被指通过约5380个虚假账号等手法转发请求、收割Claude输出，总计约1.9亿次交互，阿里以1.51亿次居首，DeepSeek虽总量较小但14天内高达1210万次，密度最高。
调查锁定DeepSeek和月之暗面，靠的不是数量而是案例细节：有被评估为疑似军方关联的用户，要求Kimi分析成都数百个警用摄像头追踪画面，月之暗面被指未经用户知情就转给了Claude。
监管逻辑发生反转：Anthropic控诉的是“我的模型输出被偷走”，网信办追究的是“中国用户数据被送出国”，同一批证据被两端各自解读，中国并未采信Anthropic的指控。
时间点极其敏感：DeepSeek本周将向联合国安理会简报AI安全风险，月之暗面正筹备香港上市，一项未结的监管调查必须写进招股说明书。
阿里三个月内第二次被指蒸馏Claude并已内部禁用Claude Code；智谱因ZCode擅自上传代码仓库致歉；小米发布最高分开源模型但未回应指控，网信办尚未公布时间表或处罚决定。
report.impact: 对AI行业，数据跨境合规正成为中美AI竞争的新战场，“蒸馏”从技术争议升级为监管议题，模型调用链条的透明度会被要求提高。对开发者，依赖海外API中转、代理调用的灰色路径风险陡增，须自查数据流向与用户告知义务。对普通用户，你在国产AI里的提问可能被静默转发到境外服务器，知情权与隐私边界问题开始被摆上台面。
report.tools: 可关注Anthropic威胁情报报告原文、网信办《数据出境安全评估办法》等跨境规则；开发者若想降低数据外流风险，可研究Qwen、GLM、Kimi K2、MiniMax等国产开源权重的本地部署方案，常用工具包括vLLM、Ollama、SGLang。
